title: Cascade Health pilot weekly - SSO, audit logs & retention sync
topics: Data retention and deletion during pilot
summary: Weekly POC sync focused on security/compliance checkpoints. Team reviewed SSO integration path, audit log retention/export options, and data retention/deletion policy for pilot. Action items assigned for SOC2 evidence, SAML test account, and audit log access for the customer's security team.
next_steps: Redwood to send SOC 2 documentation + AICPA contacts
Customer to provision SAML IdP test tenant and share metadata
Redwood SE to enable extended audit logs for pilot org and provide sample exports
Schedule deep dive on KMS/HSM integration next Wednesday
action_items: Maya: email SOC2/ISO pack and contact for audit by 2025-12-03
Liam: enable verbose audit logging on pilot org and drop sample .ndjson export into shared drive by 2025-12-04
Priya: provision SAML test tenant (Okta) and send metadata to maya@redwood.com by 2025-12-05
Noah: update pilot runbook with retention policy and delete workflow by 2025-12-06
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-12-01
Start: 15:00 PT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Liam O'Connor (Redwood SE), Noah Patel (Redwood CSM); Priya Kapoor (Cascade Head of Security), Ethan Morales (Platform Eng), Sofia Ruiz (Data Privacy), Daniel Kim (SRE)

Auto-summary: quick recap of last week's pilot metrics, then focused on security items: SSO/SAML test, audit log retention/export, data handling for pilot, SOC2 evidence requests.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): all right folks, thanks for joining, I think we have most of the same folks from last week, quick check-in on the pilot performance then we'll jump into SSO and audit stuff.
[00:18] Priya (Cascade): hi all, thanks, quick note we have the security review with internal compliance on Thursday so anything we can get earlier helps.
[00:27] Liam (Redwood SE): great, we pushed the config yesterday — latency's stable, small tuning on batching, but I've got the logs we enabled. We'll show the exports in a minute.
[00:36] Ethan (Cascade): sounds good. main ask today is can we get an SSO test flow and the full audit trail for the last 72 hours? that's what our team needs to sign off.
[00:48] Maya: yes, Priya — we'll walk through SAML test steps. Liam, you want to take the log export?
[00:52] Liam: sure. quick caveat, the verbos-verb— the verbose logs are enabled in pilot but retention is by default 30 days; for the pilot we can increase retention to 90 days but export will be the easiest immediate deliverable. I can drop an ndjson export to the shared drive with timestamps, user IDs, request ids, model id, and event types.
[01:12] Daniel (Cascade): when you say user ids are they full emails or pseudonymized? we need to avoid leaking PHI.
[01:18] Liam: good point, currently our audit lines contain the user identifier as the internal username/email; we can pseudonymize in the export or mask emails — we should align on what you need for the compliance review.
[01:27] Priya: we prefer pseudonymized exports for review, but we will need the mapping under a separate secure process if required. also, do you have SOC two artifacts? when people say SOC two I want the report.
[01:40] Maya: yes, we have SOC 2 Type II report and the AICPA letter — I will send the pack. we'll include description of control families relevant to the pilot: access controls, change management, logging, encryption in transit/at rest.
[01:55] Sofia (Cascade): and KMS — we are evaluating whether we need customer-managed keys for the pilot. can you talk to the HSM/KMS options?
[02:03] Liam: sure. for hosted pilots we support customer KMS integration via our key-wrap flow — you can bring keys from AWS KMS / GCP Cloud KMS or a vault. the runtime will encrypt model cache keys at rest with your CMK. right now, for the trial, mutual TLS plus our default managed keys are OK, but we can do an HSM proof-of-concept if needed.
[02:26] Ethan: is that a hard requirement for production or only for specific data classes?
[02:30] Maya: typically customers with high-reg needs request CMK for certain data classes. for signing and audit we have options. we'll document recommended patterns.
[02:38] [02:38] Liam: (interruption) also note — we have prefix/KV cache logs that show cache hits/misses; that doesn't include input text but does include hashed keys for cache entries.
[02:48] Priya: hashing is fine, but we need to be sure no raw patient data is persisted anywhere. what's your deletion flow?
[02:54] Liam: we have a deletion API that can remove whole trial datasets or specific job traces. for the pilot we can schedule an automated purge at end of day X and we can provide a deletion certificate — but for compliance you might want to witness or pull the logs.
[03:08] Priya: ok, we will want a deletion certificate + a sample run to prove the purge completed.
[03:14] Noah (Redwood): noted, we'll include a verifiable deletion artifact — that shows job IDs removed and timestamps, and a checksum of the export pre/post.
[03:23] Daniel: about SSO — we're on Okta. we want SAML integration so we can enforce SSO and SCIM provisioning later. timeline?
[03:32] Maya: we have a standard SAML SSO flow. Liam, can you outline steps we need from Cascade?
[03:38] Liam: sure. you (Cascade) will share the IdP metadata XML, ACS URL will be provided by us, we'll generate SP metadata; the usual: attribute mappings (email, firstName, lastName), nameid is email. for pilot we don't force SCIM but if you want we can demo SCIM for provisioning.
[03:55] Priya: any gotchas? assertion signing or encryption?
[04:00] Liam: we support signed assertions; encryption of assertion is optional. common gotcha is clock skew on Okta, so ensure NTP sync. also keep your certificate validity long enough — some test tenants rotate frequently.
[04:12] Priya: ok can you provide a test account we can try?
[04:16] Maya: yes, Maya: I'll spin up a test SP entity and share ACS/EntityID and a temp certificate.
[04:22] [04:22] (murmur)
[04:25] Maya: we'll also add a short checklist in the runbook.
[04:29] Ethan: back to audit logs — what's the granularity on request payloads? do you store full prompts in the audit trail?
[04:36] Liam: we do not include full user inputs in default audit logs; events capture metadata (request id, model, token counts, latency, user id). we can enable request payload logging in a separate opt-in bucket but for PHI you shouldn't enable payload logging.
[04:51] Sofia: makes sense. for our pilots we need the metadata and the ability to tie to a request id to see the lifecycle in tracing, not the raw content.
[04:59] Liam: yes, trace id correlation is enabled — we can link request id to infra logs without showing content.
[05:06] Priya: what about encryption at rest for cached embeddings / KV cache?
[05:10] Liam: encrypted at rest by default; cache keys are wrapped using the runtime's key material; if you bring CMK we can wrap with your key.
[05:18] Daniel: any SOC evidence for those controls?
[05:21] Maya: SOC2 report covers encryption controls and key management descriptions; the SOC auditor attested to the control operation. again, I'll send the SOC2 package.
[05:31] [05:31] Liam: quick note on audit export format — we provide ndjson with one event per line, fields: timestamp, event_type, request_id, user_id (hashed optional), model_id, tokens_in, tokens_out, latency_ms, region. can also include http headers if needed but we usually avoid that.
[05:47] Priya: will you include IP addresses? we have restrictions on storage of IPs.
[05:52] Liam: IP addresses are logged at infrastructural level; we can exclude IPs from the export. for compliance, we'll use pseudonymized user ids and drop IPs.
[06:00] Priya: good. also audit trail access — can we give read-only access to our security team?
[06:05] Maya: yes, we can create RBAC roles scoped to pilot org and give read-only log viewer role; we'll need a list of emails to invite.
[06:12] Priya: I'll send that.
[06:15] Ethan: do you have an API for pulling logs or only web UI?
[06:19] Liam: both. there's an API with pagination. export can be automated via the API or pushed to your S3. for the pilot we can push to a preconfigured S3 bucket in your account — that's usually easiest for security teams.
[06:31] Priya: push to our bucket sounds best. what about retention lifecycle on S3? we have to ensure objects auto-expire after policy.
[06:38] Liam: we can push and then you can apply lifecycle policy in your bucket. we can also configure deletion hooks to remove objects from our side after push.
[06:47] [06:47] Maya: let's align on block diagram. we'll send a short architecture note showing flow: request -> runtime -> audit log stream (redwood) -> push to customer S3 (if configured) -> retention/lifecycle managed by customer.
[07:00] Priya: thanks. next — evidence collection for SOC two, specifically change management and patching logs for the pilot nodes. we need weekly snapshots.
[07:10] Liam: we can provide patch schedule and the image IDs rolled for the pilot agents; we also have uptime/patch logs. smaller note: some of those involve internal hostnames which we'll sanitize.
[07:20] Sofia: on data residency — our legal requires logs and certain telemetry to stay in-region (EU). are you able to pin region?
[07:27] Liam: yes, we have region pinning per org; for pilot you can request EU region only and we will route logs and storage to the EU cluster. caveat: some control-plane metadata may still cross region boundaries; we'll include a note.
[07:40] Priya: ok please document that caveat.
[07:43] Maya: will do.
[07:45] Daniel: one more on RBAC — do you support custom roles?
[07:49] Liam: yes we have role templates and custom roles; you can set least-priv to only allow model inference and deny export by default; then security team can have log_viewer role.
[07:59] Priya: perfect.
[08:02] [08:02] (brief silence)
[08:05] Maya: quick pivot to the pilot metrics we promised — nothing heavy, just to confirm we didn't degrade anything while enabling verbose logs. Liam have numbers?
[08:12] Liam: latency up ~3 to 5 ms with verbose logs enabled, token cost unchanged, throughput steady. I can share the dashboard link.
[08:20] Ethan: acceptable.
[08:22] Priya: back to the deletion certificate — is that a signed doc or just a log entry?
[08:27] Noah: it's a signed JSON artifact with pre/post checksums plus a signed timestamp from our system. we can also provide a PDF if you need for audit records.
[08:35] Priya: PDF would be useful.
[08:37] Maya: we'll include both.
[08:39] Daniel: question on test data — for the pilot we will use synthetic PHI; is there a recommended way to mark test traffic?
[08:46] Liam: yes, add a header X-Test-Traffic: true and we will tag events and avoid storing payloads; we can also route to a test model variant that enforces no payload logging.
[08:58] Priya: good. about SCIM later — how long to enable?
[09:02] Liam: SCIM can be enabled in a day once you approve attribute mapping and provide admin token.
[09:08] Priya: okay.
[09:10] Maya: let's go through the explicit next steps so we close this meeting with commitments.
[09:15] Maya: item one — Maya will send SOC2 pack and runbook. item two — Liam will push audit export to your S3 and also drop pseudonymized ndjson into the shared drive. item three — Priya will provision Okta test tenant and share metadata. item four — Noah will prepare deletion certificate template.
[09:36] Priya: that's a good plan.
[09:38] Ethan: any blockers on our end? just the Okta metadata and bucket info.
[09:42] Priya: we'll get that by Friday.
[09:45] Maya: perfect, we'll target the exports by Thursday so you have artifacts before your internal review.
[09:51] [09:51] (crosstalk)
[09:53] Liam: one more technical note — if you want to test KMS wrap with your CMK, we need a short questionnaire and a limited PKI exchange; that can take a week depending on legal.
[10:05] Priya: noted — we'll prioritize if needed.
[10:08] Maya: any final Qs?
[10:10] Sofia: none from me, thank you.
[10:12] Daniel: fine.
[10:13] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up with the docs and action items in the next 48 hours.

Short recap (auto):
- SAML: Cascade to provide Okta metadata; Redwood to provide SP details and test account.
- Audit logs: Redwood to enable verbose logs for pilot, pseudonymize user ids, push ndjson export to customer S3 and shared drive.
- Deletion: Redwood to provide deletion certificate and sample proof-of-purge.
- SOC2: Redwood to share SOC2 Type II and related artifacts.

Links/Artifacts referenced:
- Pilot dashboard: https://app.redwood.ai/orgs/cascade/pilot-dashboard (demo link)
- Shared drive: https://drive.firecloud.example/reports/cascade-pilot-logs (placeholder)
- SOC2 pack (to be sent)

End of transcript.
